IL‐17A is a key cytokine that is required for the development of the inflammatory response to S. aureus in the lung.

IL‐17‐producing cells in the peripheral blood are heterogeneous and can be subdivided into two distinct populations, Th17 and Th1‐17 cells, based on their expression of the transcription factors RORγt and T‐bet, respectively.
Th17 cells are not only pathogenic, but they also have a role in the maintenance of intestinal homeostasis, and their absence can lead to spontaneous colitis.
